articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually uploaded AWS GovCloud keys to GitHub like it's a public mixtape. The agency that's supposed to protect our infrastructure just doxxed itself harder than Anonymous ever could.

articles.title: 23andMe inherits lawsuit over 'disturbing' DNA data breach
articles.summary: Critical RCE in Gogs has been sitting unfixed since March while maintainers ghost the researcher. Exploit module is live and ready to party.

articles.title: Dutch cops wrest 17M devices from mystery botnet's clutches
articles.summary: 23andMe gets sued for downplaying their DNA data breach while allegedly paying ransom to attackers. Your genetic privacy sold for crypto coins — dystopia achieved.

articles.title: ChatGPhish Vulnerability Turns ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface
articles.summary: PAN-OS authentication bypass (CVE-2026-0257) is being actively exploited in the wild. Palo Alto's firewall just became a welcome mat.

articles.title: Microsoft faces security community backlash over Nightmare Eclipse
articles.summary: Microsoft threatens legal action against researcher Nightmare Eclipse for disclosing exploits. Because apparently shooting the messenger is easier than fixing Windows.

articles.title: More License Plate Reader Mission Creep: School Residency Verification, Background Checks, and Noise Complaints
articles.summary: Age verification systems are turning into a privacy apocalypse for everyone online. Lawmakers trying to protect kids just built the surveillance state's wet dream.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: Police are using license plate readers for everything from school residency checks to noise complaints. Mission creep meets surveillance state in America's parking lots.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF scores a win for encrypted messaging, keeping our digital conversations safe from government voyeurs. Sometimes the good guys actually win one.

articles.title: ICE to keep an eye on your eyes under $25M biometric scanner deal
articles.summary: Lone attacker published 14 malicious npm packages mimicking OpenSearch and Elasticsearch libraries. Supply chain attacks just got more personal.

articles.title: New Russia-Linked GREYVIBE Targets Ukraine with AI-Powered Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Attackers exploited Marimo CVE-2026-39987 then deployed an LLM agent for post-compromise activities. AI is now helping hackers clean up after themselves — the future is weird.
